subject: Nebula Dynamics — traffic diary & peak mapping for Dedicated sizing
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit@nebuladyn.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nebuladyn.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Nebula Dynamics — traffic diary & peak mapping for Dedicated sizing

Hi Amit / Elena,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — excited about Nebula Dynamics potentially using Redwood Dedicated for inference. To size a reliable Dedicated footprint we need a short longitudinal view of your traffic so our pre-sales sizing can propose a fleet that matches both sustained needs and peak windows.

I've attached a simple CSV template (nebuladyn_traffic_diary.csv) to make this quick. Can you and Elena fill out the following for a representative 10–14 day period (UTC timestamps preferred):

- per-minute request counts (or 5/15m buckets)
- average prompt tokens and average response tokens per request
- 50/90/99 token-length percentiles for both prompt and response
- concurrency as measured at the API (inflight requests) per 5m bucket
- a flag for session-bound requests vs one-off calls (approx %)
- percent of requests that are streaming vs non-streaming
- any dayparting (business hours, global spikes) and timezone for your peak windows
- retry behavior (do you retry at client level? retry rates %)

Optional but super helpful: sample prompt/response pairs (anonymized) and a short note about target p99 latency SLO and any regulatory retention constraints.

What we'll do after we get this diary: run a capacity simulation that maps to GPU SKUs (2x A100/RTX-class equivalents), suggest batching/prefix-caching profiles, and propose a conservative canary commit for the first month. If you can return the CSV by EOD Monday Nov 9 that gives us time to simulate before our call next week.

Attachments: nebuladyn_traffic_diary.csv (template), prompt_response_samples_instructions.txt

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Redwood Inference | Production-first inference platform
From: Amit Rao <amit@nebuladyn.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nebuladyn.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nebula Dynamics — traffic diary & peak mapping for Dedicated sizing

Kimberly, thanks — this looks straightforward. I've asked Elena to pull logs; attaching a first-pass CSV (nebuladyn_traffic_diary.csv) and a short note about how we bucket tokens.

Quick clarifications:
- Our timestamps in logs are PST; do you want them converted to UTC or is local OK?
- We have a spike pattern tied to nightly batch jobs that fan out many short calls between 02:00-03:00 PST — should those be treated as "peak" for sizing or backlogable? They are latency-insensitive but bursty.
- We use client-side retries only on 5xx; retry rate ~0.7% over last month.

Attachments: nebuladyn_traffic_diary.csv (filled draft), prompt_response_samples.zip (anonymized pairs)

Amit Rao
CTO, Nebula Dynamics
amit@nebuladyn.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Nebula Dynamics traffic diary received — next steps

Kim — pulling the draft Amit sent. High-level thoughts:

- The nightly 02:00-03:00 PST batch spikes look safe to treat as backlog-able for strict latency SLOs, but they will drive short-term GPU occupancy. We should model two configs: (A) peak-aware with burst pool (oversubscribe + preemptible GPUs) and (B) conservative dedicated commit sized for observed day peaks.
- Token distribution: median prompt ~40 tokens, median response ~280, but 99th response token is ~1800 — that long-tail will change memory footprint and KV cache needs.
- Concurrency stable during business hours ~120 inflight, peaks to ~900 for 3–5 minute bursts.

Action items I can take:
1) Run baseline sim using current token distribution + two SKU mixes (8x 80GB, 16x 40GB) and produce a cost/latency estimate.
2) Draft a short canary rollout plan that uses autoscaling windows and a fallback to a smaller model during peak.
3) Prepare a short slide that maps their p99 target to expected queueing at each SKU mix.

I'll kick off the sim if you want me to. Also recommend we schedule a 30-min sizing review with Amit + Elena next Tue (Nov 16) to walk through results.

Marissa
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit@nebuladyn.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nebuladyn.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nebula Dynamics — traffic diary & peak mapping for Dedicated sizing

Amit / Elena — appreciate the quick turnaround and the sample CSV. Marissa and I reviewed and started the baseline sims. Two small asks before the call:

1) Please confirm whether the nightly batch spike is OK to treat as backlogable (i.e., can be served with a longer latency window) or if you want sub-200ms p99 even for those calls.
2) If you have any retention or audit log constraints (KMS/HSM keys, SOC2 contract clauses) call them out now so we factor them into the Private/Dedicated tradeoffs.

I've shared a short workbook with preliminary graphs here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Xy-traffic-samples — Marissa will present the simulation outputs on the sizing call. Proposed meeting: Tue Nov 16, 11:00 PT / 19:00 UTC — I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Next steps after the call: formal SKU recommendation, a month-1 conservative commit + burst pool design, and an ops runbook for canarying.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
